title: Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act

claims.claim: Federal tax law normally requires casualty losses to exceed 10% of income before they can be deducted.
claims.sourceSpan: as exceeds 10 percent of the adjusted gross income of the individual
claims.note: 10% AGI floor mechanism appears verbatim; the new special rule is written as an exception to it.

claims.claim: Congress has repeatedly carved out exceptions for federally declared disaster areas.
claims.sourceSpan: section 70438 of Public Law
claims.note: Background generalization; supported structurally by the bill coordinating with two prior disaster-tax provisions (304(b) of the 2020 Act and section 70438 of PL 119-21) plus the extended HR 5863. 'repeatedly' is historical framing, not a per-line fact.

claims.claim: Affected taxpayers may deduct unreimbursed losses above $500 per incident.
claims.sourceSpan: $100 ($500 in the case of any qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses
claims.note: $500 per-casualty floor for qualified disaster-related losses verbatim; 'per incident' glosses 'per casualty'.

claims.claim: These losses are unreimbursed.
claims.sourceSpan: not compensated for by insurance or otherwise
claims.note: 'unreimbursed' is a standard characterization of casualty-loss deductibility; the insurance-offset condition is stated verbatim in the wildfire definition.

claims.claim: The deduction is available even without itemizing.
claims.sourceSpan: Deduction allowed to individuals who do not elect to itemize deductions
claims.note: Section 2(c) header verbatim; new 63(b)(8) makes the disaster loss deductible for non-itemizers.

claims.claim: Applies to disasters with incident periods beginning on or after December 28, 2019.
claims.sourceSpan: begins on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027

claims.claim: Applies to disasters with incident periods before January 1, 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: begins on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027

claims.claim: Extends the exclusion of wildfire relief payments from taxable income.
claims.sourceSpan: Gross income shall not include any amount received by an individual as a qualified wildfire relief payment

claims.claim: For forest or range fires.
claims.sourceSpan: as a result of any forest or range fire

claims.claim: Federally declared a disaster after 2014.
claims.sourceSpan: declared after December 31, 2014
claims.note: 'after 2014' glosses 'after December 31, 2014'.

claims.claim: And before 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: and before January 1, 2027, as a result of any forest or range fire
claims.note: 'before 2027' glosses 'before January 1, 2027'.

claims.claim: Wildfire exclusion extended to payments received in tax years 2026 and later.
claims.sourceSpan: payments received in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025
claims.note: Payments received in taxable years beginning after Dec 31, 2025 = tax year 2026 onward.

claims.claim: Extends the federal tax deduction for disaster property losses.
claims.sourceSpan: codify and extend the rules for personal casualty losses arising from major disasters
claims.note: 'property losses' glosses 'personal casualty losses'.

claims.claim: And the wildfire relief payment exclusion.
claims.sourceSpan: exclusion from gross income of compensation for losses or damages resulting from certain wildfires

claims.claim: To disasters occurring before January 1, 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: before January 1, 2027
claims.note: Both the casualty and wildfire windows end before January 1, 2027.

claims.claim: Disaster Loss Deductions.
claims.sourceSpan: Codification and extension of rules for casualty losses arising from major disasters
claims.note: Label for the Sec 2 casualty-loss provision.

claims.claim: Applies to disasters with incident periods beginning on or after December 28, 2019.
claims.sourceSpan: begins on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027

claims.claim: And before January 1, 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: begins on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027

claims.claim: Deductible without itemizing.
claims.sourceSpan: Deduction allowed to individuals who do not elect to itemize deductions

claims.claim: Disaster loss exempt from the 10% income floor.
claims.sourceSpan: as exceeds 10 percent of the adjusted gross income of the individual
claims.note: The qualified net disaster loss is added on top of the amount exceeding 10% AGI, so the disaster loss itself is not reduced by the 10% floor.

claims.claim: Wildfire Relief Payments.
claims.sourceSpan: Compensation for losses or damages resulting from certain wildfires
claims.note: Label for the Sec 3 / 139M provision.

claims.claim: Relief payments for forest or range fires.
claims.sourceSpan: as a result of any forest or range fire

claims.claim: Federally declared a disaster after 2014 and before 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: declared after December 31, 2014, and before January 1, 2027

claims.claim: Excluded from gross income.
claims.sourceSpan: Gross income shall not include any amount received by an individual as a qualified wildfire relief payment

claims.claim: Exclusion now covers payments received in tax years 2026 and later.
claims.sourceSpan: payments received in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025

claims.claim: Prior law covered payments received in tax years 2020 through 2025.
claims.sourceSpan: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2019, and before January 1, 2026
claims.note: REFERENCED SOURCE bill-118-hr-5863: prior-law window = taxable years beginning after Dec 31, 2019 and before Jan 1, 2026 = tax years 2020-2025.

claims.claim: Names the Act the "Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act".
claims.sourceSpan: Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act

claims.claim: Short-title section - citation name only; no substantive effect.
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the
claims.note: Structural characterization of a short-title section.

claims.claim: Adds Section 165(h)(6) to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 165(h) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph
claims.note: 165(h) amended by adding new paragraph (6).

claims.claim: Creating a special deduction category for qualified net disaster losses.
claims.sourceSpan: (6) Special rule for qualified net disaster losses

claims.claim: That bypasses the 10% adjusted gross income limitation.
claims.sourceSpan: as exceeds 10 percent of the adjusted gross income of the individual
claims.note: The qualified net disaster loss is deductible in full, added to the amount exceeding 10% AGI.

claims.claim: A qualified net disaster loss is the excess of qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses over personal casualty gains.
claims.sourceSpan: qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses, over
claims.note: Source: excess of (i) qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses over (ii) personal casualty gains (reduced per 5(B)(i), a detail the analysis simplifies).

claims.claim: A qualified disaster area covers any area with a presidential major disaster declaration under section 401 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act.
claims.sourceSpan: a major disaster has been declared by the President under section 401 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act

claims.claim: Where the incident period begins on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: begins on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027

claims.claim: Individuals who do not itemize may deduct the loss through new Section 63(b)(8).
claims.sourceSpan: so much of the deduction allowed by section 165(a) as is attributable to the qualified net disaster loss
claims.note: Section 63(b) amended by adding paragraph (8); non-itemizer deduction.

claims.claim: The per-casualty floor is $500 for qualified disaster-related losses (versus $100 otherwise).
claims.sourceSpan: $100 ($500 in the case of any qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses
claims.note: Post-amendment 165(h)(1): $100 general floor, $500 for qualified disaster-related losses. Direction correct.

claims.claim: And the amendments apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.
claims.sourceSpan: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024

claims.claim: Creates new Section 139M of the Internal Revenue Code.
claims.sourceSpan: 139M. Compensation for losses or damages resulting from certain wildfires

claims.claim: Excluding qualified wildfire relief payments from gross income.
claims.sourceSpan: Gross income shall not include any amount received by an individual as a qualified wildfire relief payment

claims.claim: The exclusion applies to payments for forest or range fires federally declared a disaster after December 31, 2014, and before January 1, 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: declared after December 31, 2014, and before January 1, 2027, as a result of any forest or range fire

claims.claim: And covers payments received in taxable years after December 31, 2025 with no stated end year.
claims.sourceSpan: payments received in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025
claims.note: Enrolled 139M has no payment-received end-date limitation subsection, so 'no stated end year' is accurate.

claims.claim: Under prior law, the exclusion applied only to qualifying payments received in taxable years after December 31, 2019 and before January 1, 2026.
claims.sourceSpan: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2019, and before January 1, 2026
claims.note: REFERENCED SOURCE bill-118-hr-5863 Sec 3(d) verbatim window.

claims.claim: Section 304(b) of the Taxpayer Certainty and Disaster Tax Relief Act of 2020 is made inapplicable to any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2024.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 304(b) of the Taxpayer Certainty and Disaster Tax Relief Act of 2020

claims.claim: Section 70438 of Public Law 119-21 is made inapplicable to any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2024.
claims.sourceSpan: section 70438 of Public Law

claims.claim: Both are made inapplicable to any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2024.
claims.sourceSpan: shall not apply to any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2024
claims.note: 'made inapplicable' = 'shall not apply'.

claims.claim: The section is captioned as codification and extension of casualty-loss rules, but this subsection deactivates two prior-law disaster-loss provisions, so the new rules replace rather than stack on the earlier ones.
claims.sourceSpan: Codification and extension of rules for casualty losses arising from major disasters
claims.note: Caption verbatim; the coordination rule turns off the two prior provisions for post-2024 years - accurate structural read.

claims.claim: The bill covers disasters with incident periods beginning before January 1, 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: begins on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027

claims.claim: But does not address losses within a qualified disaster area where the damage is discovered or claims are settled after January 1, 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: begins on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027
claims.note: Accurate statement of a scope boundary; eligibility keys off the incident period's begin date, so a loss from a qualifying incident period is covered regardless of discovery/settlement date.

claims.claim: The wildfire relief exclusion applies only to fires paired with a federal disaster declaration.
claims.sourceSpan: any Federally declared disaster (as defined in section 165(i)(5)(A)) declared after December 31, 2014

claims.claim: And does not address relief payments from state programs for fires that did not receive a federal declaration.
claims.sourceSpan: any Federally declared disaster (as defined in section 165(i)(5)(A)) declared after December 31, 2014
claims.note: Accurate statement of absence; a federal declaration is a definitional requirement.

claims.claim: Section 165(h)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code - qualified net disaster loss deduction bypassing the 10% AGI limitation.
claims.sourceSpan: (6) Special rule for qualified net disaster losses

claims.claim: Section 63(b)(8) - deduction for the qualified net disaster loss available to individuals who do not itemize.
claims.sourceSpan: so much of the deduction allowed by section 165(a) as is attributable to the qualified net disaster loss

claims.claim: Section 139M - exclusion from gross income for qualified wildfire relief payments for forest or range fires federally declared a disaster after December 31, 2014 and before January 1, 2027 (for payments received in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025).
claims.sourceSpan: declared after December 31, 2014, and before January 1, 2027, as a result of any forest or range fire
claims.note: Section 139M, declaration window, and Sec 3(c) effective date all verbatim in source.

claims.claim: Section 165(h)(1) per-casualty floor - $100 generally, $500 for qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses.
claims.sourceSpan: $100 ($500 in the case of any qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses

claims.claim: Definition of qualified disaster area - incident periods beginning on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027.
claims.sourceSpan: begins on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027

claims.claim: Section 304(b) of the Taxpayer Certainty and Disaster Tax Relief Act of 2020 and section 70438 of Public Law 119-21 made inapplicable to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.
claims.sourceSpan: shall not apply to any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2024
claims.note: 'removed' = the two prior provisions are made inapplicable for post-2024 tax years; entities and date verbatim.

claims.claim: This bill extends disaster tax relief that Congress enacted in the prior session.
claims.sourceSpan: Federal Disaster Tax Relief Act of 2023
claims.note: Structural: the extended measure (HR 5863 / Federal Disaster Tax Relief Act, PL 118-148) is a prior-Congress enactment (referenced source).

claims.claim: Applying the existing casualty-loss deduction and wildfire-payment exclusion to more recent disasters rather than creating a new program.
claims.sourceSpan: codify and extend the rules for personal casualty losses arising from major disasters
claims.note: Accurate structural characterization; the bill codifies and extends existing rules.

claims.claim: Its nationwide scope covers presidentially declared disasters in any state.
claims.sourceSpan: a major disaster has been declared by the President under section 401 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act
claims.note: Structural: qualified disaster area = any area with a presidential major-disaster declaration (nationwide).

notes: Amendment bill (enrolled text, 87 lines) that codifies + extends two disaster-tax provisions of the Internal Revenue Code, drawing prior-law figures from referenced source bill-118-hr-5863 (Federal Disaster Tax Relief Act, PL 118-148). All figures (10% AGI, $100/$500 per-casualty floor, Dec 28 2019, Jan 1 2027, Dec 31 2014, Dec 31 2024, Dec 31 2025, prior-law 2020-2025 window), entities (165(h)(6), 63(b)(8), 139M, section 401 Stafford Act, 304(b) of the 2020 Act, section 70438 of PL 119-21), and directions (add deduction, exclude from gross income, deduct without itemizing, provisions made inapplicable) verify against source. No material errors - consistent with today's cross-model source-verify that found the bill clean after a likelihoodReason rewrite. Flagged (all minor, status open): likelihoodReason class-8 style debt (no-opposition / both-parties-support / Republican sponsor / 14 cosponsors / low-cost / little-organized-opposition - metadata or editorial, not in bill text); plus two minor coverage omissions (139M(c) denial-of-double-benefit and the 139M(b)(1) insurance-offset limitation). Non-material technical provisions not separately flagged: the Sec 3(b) clerical table-of-sections amendment and the 165(h)(6)(C)(iv) FEMA incident-period definition. Quote rows SKIPPED: the House-floor Congressional Record containing the four featured_quotes (Steube, Panetta, Fong, Tokuda) is not in the local corpus - cr_raw.json holds only a Senate procedural entry (2026-08-07) that names the bill but not the quotes - so quote text/stance/bioguide could not be verified against source. Stage 'Passed Senate' is consistent with the enrolled text (cleared both chambers); votes[] holds only duplicate House voice-vote rows, no stage-vs-vote contradiction.
